name: across-1
statement: The base's long-answer failures (low-temperature loops, cap hits, inability to continue its own long prefix) come from early-to-mid-layer self-copying of its own earlier reasoning by induction-driven repeat circuitry (attention heads from layer 7 and repeat-reading MLP neurons in layers 10-15), and the cap-hit part of RL's gain is a diffuse, task-general weakening of that self-copy pathway in layers 0-15, which temperature, restarts and an RL-written prefix each partly substitute for.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math on MATH-500 and the 328, cap 16,384, T 0.6 and T 1.0. Covers the cap-hit and loop share of the gap and the layer location of the weight change that removes it. Does not cover the non-cap errors at T 1.0 (misreads, arithmetic slips, wrong method), nor the 'Answer:' format change.

explains.how: At T 0.6 the base's sharpened distribution lets the self-copy attractor win, so most cap hits are verbatim loops.

explains.quote: T 1.0 / top-p 1.0: 410/500 MATH-500 (82.0 %), grader v3, 27 cap hits
explains.how: Temperature 1.0 breaks the copy attractor by sampling off the copied token, removing most loops without changing the weights.
The same temperature effect on loops appears in an unrelated model, as expected if loops are a generic copy attractor rather than a math deficit.

explains.quote: from RL's prefix 48 / 41 / 21; from its own prefix 23 / 16 / 38
explains.how: The base finishes twice as often from RL's prefix: its own prefix contains the repeated material that its copy circuitry locks onto.

explains.quote: partly because it cannot continue its own long solution
explains.how: Self-conditioning on its own long text, not missing knowledge, is the failure.

explains.quote: counts peak at layers 10-15 (121-171 per layer)
explains.how: The repeat-reading neurons that would drive self-copying sit in the same layer band where the effective RL change sits.

explains.quote: The best set sits in layers 1-15
explains.how: Attribution-ranked RL neurons concentrate in the induction/repeat band, as predicted if the decisive change acts on copying.

explains.quote: MLP layers 0-15 carry about twice what 16-31 do
explains.how: Early-layer delta closes twice the KL of late-layer delta, matching an early-mid-layer mechanism.

explains.quote: the +3.4 difference lies entirely in cap-hit problems
explains.how: Adding the MLP delta on top of attention changes only cap-hit problems: the loop/cap share needs the MLP repeat neurons, not only the induction heads.

explains.quote: on the longest, cap hits fall 32.8 points and accuracy holds
explains.how: For the plain base, temperature removes cap hits on the longest problems, where self-copy has the most own text to copy.
RL no longer depends on temperature to escape copying because the pathway itself is weakened.

explains.quote: the base hit the cap on 16 and finished with a wrong answer on 33
explains.how: Only the cap-hit third of the 328 gap is in scope; the theory predicts that layer 0-15 edits recover these 16 and not the 33.

conflicts.quote: diverge on math solutions, more with depth
conflicts.how: Activation divergence grows with depth (largest in layers 24-31), whereas the theory places the decisive change in layers 0-15.

conflicts.quote: Late-MLP top directions x base lm_head read as deliberation words
conflicts.how: The most structured part of the delta reads out in late layers as deliberation tokens, a late-layer mechanism.

conflicts.quote: Rule-A loops: 0 of 500 in either cell
conflicts.how: At T 1.0 there are no loops yet a 10.6-point gap remains; the theory only covers the cap-hit share, and 16 non-loop cap hits must be explained as drift, not verbatim copying.

conflicts.quote: RL barely moves which tokens a neuron fires on most
conflicts.how: If RL weakened repeat neurons broadly, their top contexts might shift; the theory needs the change to be a rescaling, which the top-50 test ignores.
On the base's cap hits RL's largest early differences are deliberation tokens, suggesting a stop/deliberate control rather than copy suppression.

rival: RL's gain is a late-layer budget/stop controller learned from 3.1's truncation-as-negative training (across-2). Separation: copy the RL delta of layers 0-15 only vs layers 16-31 only into the cued base at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95; this theory predicts the 0-15 arm removes most cap hits and the 16-31 arm removes few, the rival predicts the reverse. A second separator: the repeat-neuron response to repeated random tokens (non-math input) is weaker in RL under this theory and unchanged under the rival.

predictions.experiment: Base + RL delta in layers 0-15 only (all tensors of those layers, rest base), opening cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3: cap hits
predictions.refuted_by: Cap hits >= 80, or the layers 16-31 arm has fewer cap hits than this arm

predictions.experiment: Base + RL delta in layers 16-31 only, opening cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3: cap hits
predictions.refuted_by: Cap hits <= 60 (late layers alone remove most loops)

predictions.experiment: 4fb5eb protocol (512 repeated random-token sequences) run on Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math: second-pass rise of the base's top-100 repeat neurons, RL divided by base
predictions.refuted_by: Ratio >= 0.95 (RL's repeat response on non-math input is unchanged)

predictions.experiment: Base + (Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code - base), opening cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3: cap hits
predictions.refuted_by: Cap hits >= 110 (an orthogonal RL delta from another task does not weaken looping)

predictions.experiment: RL model continuing the cued base's own T 0.6 looping answers (92 low-ratio cap hits), prefix cut one repeated block after the rule-A onset, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384 total: fraction that finish without a cap hit
predictions.refuted_by: RL finishes < 0.3 of them (RL is captured by the same repeated prefix)
